scenario: Floa Reader EPUB highlight add, restore model, and live removal

reference.source: Glaso public guided animation, Reader lesson
observedUserActions: Select a passage in an EPUB
Save the passage as a highlight
See the highlight on the current page
reference.fidelity: Behavioral comparison only; no Glaso code, binaries, or assets used.

application.runtime: Chrome headless against the extracted macOS arm64 app.asar over loopback HTTP
application.persistenceBridge: Stubbed; renderer and EPUB.js were not stubbed

observations.step: Select text in the EPUB iframe
observations.evidence: epub.js produced an epubcfi(/6/2!/4/6,/1:0,/1:27) range and the Reader enabled Highlight.

observations.step: Save and show the highlight without reopening the book
observations.evidence: The mocked persistence bridge returned a saved highlight; the live rendition registered a reader-saved-highlight mark with fill #ffe58a and fill-opacity 0.55. The screenshot shows the selected passage highlighted on the current page.

observations.step: Clear the EPUB selection after saving
observations.evidence: The iframe selection and temporary renderer selection state were cleared after the highlight was applied.

observations.step: Switch to another book and reopen the EPUB
observations.evidence: The renderer reconstructed the saved epub.js mark from the persisted highlight metadata when the EPUB was opened again.

observations.step: Keep a search query while switching documents and refresh its result
observations.evidence: A phrase with no match in the PDF remained in the search field; after opening the EPUB, the Reader searched the new document and displayed its match instead of keeping the previous document's result state.

observations.step: Remove the highlight while the EPUB remains open
observations.evidence: The bridge accepted removal and epub.js removed the annotation from the live rendition registry without reopening the document.

limitations: The persistence bridge was mocked; this does not verify on-disk persistence or restart restoration.
The fixture is generated for this run rather than a Glaso document.
No Electron BrowserWindow was created, no app was activated, and the existing Just Browse process was left untouched.
